sections.title: LAN in One Line
sections.body: A LAN is a network that lives inside ONE small place — your home, one office floor, or a school building. It is private (you own it), very fast, and everything is close together.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
sections.body: The switch connects your devices. The router is the exit door to the outside world:
sections.code:
[PC] [PC] [Printer]
   \   |   /
   [ Switch ]   <-- this whole thing = LAN
        |
    [ Router ] ---> outside world (WAN / Internet)

sections.title: LAN vs WAN
sections.body: LAN = inside your walls. WAN = the long-distance link between LANs (usually rented from an internet provider).

sections.title: What Lives Inside a LAN
points: End devices — PCs, laptops, printers, IP phones, cameras.
Router — the way out to other networks.
Wi-Fi access point — same LAN, just without wires.
Optional firewall — a security guard at the door.

sections.title: When One LAN Is Not Enough
sections.body: If 500 devices share one flat LAN, everyone hears every broadcast shout — it gets noisy and slow. Big companies cut the LAN into smaller virtual pieces called VLANs (you will meet them later in this course).
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: LAN = small area + high speed + privately owned. If a question says "campus network owned by the company", it is a LAN.
